paragraphs.source_en: A group of Central Saharan engravings called Kel Essuf is not included in the classical stylistic sequence. Even though the group was already known of in the 1960s (Mori 1967) it has been virtually ignored until recently (Striedter et al. 2002-3). Unlike Bubaline engravings, the Kel Essuf are found near to, or in the same shelters as those adorned by Round Head paintings and several superimpositions indicate that these engravings are older than the Round Head paintings.

units.source_en: Unlike Bubaline engravings, the Kel Essuf are found near to, or in the same shelters as those adorned by Round Head paintings and several superimpositions indicate that these engravings are older than the Round Head paintings.

paragraphs.source_en: The Round Head paintings are concentrated in four main areas: The northwestern Tassili, Tassili Plateau, Acacus and Algerian Tadrart. They are spatially separated from the Bubaline engravings which mainly occupy the extreme north of the Tassili, the borders of the Tassili, Algerian Tadrart and Acacus and they are mainly concentrated outside the Round Head area, in the Messak, east of the Acacus. Bubaline engravings are very rare on the Tassili Plateau which is dominated by Round Heads. These two styles are more closely present in the Acacus and Algerian Tadrart but they usually occupy different sites. The Pastoral engravings are present in the same sites as the Bubaline engravings; the paintings of the Pastoral style may coexist with Round Head paintings in the same sites but they are also present in different sites.
